# Prefix integration V92: divergent clients, long followups and real vision

Frozen build succeeds through the corrected model-lock-holding driver. Runtime prefix behavior is unchanged from V89; the source comment contract is corrected and the new diagnostics extend integration coverage. Plain/MTP retention tests pass146/152assertions, including three divergent suffix lengths17/259/1795(2051total prompt tokens), a distinct auxiliary request after each, exact output against same-boundary independent references and preservation of the common checkpoint. MTP validation additionally rejects a deliberately missing alignment row without evicting a prior checkpoint.

Real vision passes32plain and42MTP assertions. Bounded real PNG fixtures with identical token geometry but different pixels are decoded, resized and processed through the actual tower plus all48language layers. Two cases place the image wholly before the256token checkpoint or crossing it. Five request preparations per case cover independent reference, initial checkpoint creation, exact fork reuse, changed-image reference and changed-image miss. SHA256 of every represented state tensor's dtype/shape/payload and full continued logits must match the independent reference. Fully covered images skip the tower; partial images re-encode the whole image and consume the correct suffix rows. Changed pixels with the same placeholder IDs refuse the old prefix. Every MTP committed state retains exact alignment. All372assertions pass. These correctness runs are not comparative latency or sampled-peak evidence; the diagnostic checks bounded endpoints under10GB.

An independent seven-pair serving confirmation is frozen separately with the unchanged minimum-five-clean/exact-output/5percent/80percent-positive/memory/nominal-power criteria and a symmetric60second before-cell cooldown. This defines an intermittent-request regime; it is not replacement of V89 exclusions and has no result at this source capture. The embedding-row component under preparation is not part of this V92 frozen binary or an enabled runtime path.
